title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke. METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter. RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047). CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings. EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Mitochondrial LONP1: Linking structure and function to context‑dependent roles in disease (Review).
abstract: Mitochondrial proteostasis is essential for maintaining organellar integrity, metabolic adaptation and cellular survival under physiological and stress conditions. Among mitochondrial quality control mechanisms, Lon peptidase 1 (LONP1) is an ATP‑dependent AAA+ serine protease localized predominantly in the mitochondrial matrix and plays a central role in the recognition and degradation of damaged or misfolded proteins. Recent structural, molecular and multi‑omics studies have expanded our understanding of LONP1 beyond proteolysis, implicating it in protein quality control, mitochondrial DNA maintenance, metabolic regulation and responses to oxidative and cellular stress. Increasing evidence also indicates that LONP1 functions are highly dependent on cellular and disease context, with both loss and gain of LONP1 activity associated with distinct pathological outcomes. The present review integrated recent structural and functional advances to establish a structure‑function framework for understanding how LONP1 coordinates proteolytic and chaperone‑like activities and how these functions are shaped by cellular and disease context. The present review further examined its roles in metabolic, neurodegenerative, reproductive, cardiovascular and malignant diseases, with particular emphasis on the context‑dependent consequences of LONP1 dysregulation and its emerging therapeutic potential. Finally, the present review highlighted unresolved questions concerning substrate recognition and specificity, the relative contributions of protease and chaperone‑like functions, disease‑specific directionality and the safety and feasibility of therapeutic modulation. These challenges need to be addressed to establish the functional and translational boundaries of LONP1.

title: Microplastic Detection in the Ascending Aorta: An Exploratory Study Using Pyrolysis-Gas Chromatography/Mass Spectrometry (Py-GC/MS).
abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as significant environmental pollutants that have been detected in various human tissues. This pilot biomonitoring study explored polymer mass in dissected versus non-dissected ascending aortic tissue. A total of 16 ascending aortic samples (8 acute type A aortic dissection [AD] and 8 acute type B dissection with arch involvement but a non-dissected ascending aorta [ND]) were examined using pyrolysis-gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) to screen 11 polymers. Both groups had aortic disease. Polymer-related signals were reported in all samples, with total mass estimates ranging from 1.92 to 155.58 µg/g tissue. The predominant reported polymer was polyamide 66 (PA66; 50.7%), followed by polyvinyl chloride (PVC; 40.5%) and polyethylene terephthalate (PET; 8.8%). AD tissues showed a 3.9-fold higher estimated polymer burden than ND tissues (74.51 ± 42.81 vs. 19.25 ± 16.48 µg/g, p = 0.0077). PET estimates were also higher in AD tissues (7.36 ± 6.44 vs. 0.89 ± 1.49 µg/g, p = 0.025), but PET identification was tentative and polymer-specific tests were exploratory. Total polymer mass correlated with ascending aortic diameter (Spearman's rho = 0.865, p < 0.001). The age- and group-adjusted association (coefficient 0.079 mm per µg/g; p = 0.0098) was sensitive to omission of one observation (p = 0.140). These findings describe a difference in estimated polymer burden between two diseased-tissue groups. Incomplete analytical validation and possible perioperative contamination limit interpretation; particle identity, tissue localization, vascular toxicity and causality were not established. Further analytical and multicenter validation is needed.

title: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits: a case report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Stanford type A aortic dissection (AAD) constitutes a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Painless AAD manifesting exclusively as isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits represents an uncommon but recognised presentation of aortic dissection that is prone to misdiagnosis. This case report adds real-world clinical data regarding atypical AAD and delivers practical diagnostic and surgical insights for front-line clinicians. MAIN SYMPTOMS AND IMPORTANT CLINICAL FINDINGS: A 58-year-old Han Chinese female presented with acute-onset bilateral lower-limb numbness and weakness lasting one hour, in the absence of chest, back or abdominal pain. Physical examination uncovered an inter-arm systolic blood-pressure discrepancy together with bilateral lower-limb motor weakness (3/5). Emergency non-contrast chest-abdominal CT identified the aortic double-lumen sign and inward-displaced aortic wall calcified plaques, whereas bilateral distal peripheral pulses remained preserved. MAIN DIAGNOSES, THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS, AND OUTCOMES: Painless Stanford type A aortic dissection complicated by suspected transient spinal cord malperfusion was diagnosed. Following urgent inter-hospital transfer, the patient underwent emergency Bentall procedure combined with aortic arch reconstruction and frozen elephant-trunk graft implantation, with a distal landing zone in the proximal descending thoracic aorta. Her bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits had fully resolved by postoperative day 2. A residual chronic dissection with a thrombosed false lumen persisted distally below the stent-graft and remained stable without interval enlargement. Six-month follow-up confirmed complete functional recovery without residual neurological sequelae or proximal dissection recurrence. CONCLUSION: Undiagnosed painless Stanford type A aortic dissection presenting with isolated bilateral lower-limb neurological deficits is associated with substantial mortality. Routine bilateral upper-arm blood-pressure measurement and recognition of calcification displacement signs on non-contrast CT facilitate early clinical suspicion. Timely confirmation by CTA and urgent comprehensive surgical reconstruction are essential to reverse end-organ malperfusion and optimize neurological as well as survival outcomes.

title: Fixed-Dose Combination Versus Add-On Therapy: Clarifying the Role of Cilostazol-Rosuvastatin in Peripheral Artery Disease.
abstract: The randomized trial by Kemalasari et al. provides evidence supporting the addition of cilostazol to rosuvastatin in patients with symptomatic peripheral artery disease. However, because the study compared the fixed-dose combination (FDC) with rosuvastatin plus placebo, it does not establish whether the FDC formulation offers advantages over an equivalent free-combination regimen. Evidence from other cardiovascular settings suggests that FDC formulations may improve medication adherence and treatment persistence, although their effects on long-term clinical outcomes remain uncertain. Future randomized studies directly comparing fixed-dose and free-combination regimens, with adherence assessed over 12 months and longer-term cardiovascular and limb outcomes evaluated, are needed to clarify the clinical value of the formulation itself.

title: Deep Vein Thrombosis Complicated by the Dissemination of Muscular Tuberculosis due to Acupuncture Treatment.
abstract: ObjectivesTo present a rare case of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in the right upper extremity caused by muscular tuberculosis (MTB), likely disseminated via acupuncture, and to describe the diagnostic and therapeutic challenges encountered.MethodsThis case report details the clinical presentation, diagnostic workup, and management of a patient with MTB-associated DVT. The patient was treated with standard anti-tuberculosis therapy (rifampicin, isoniazid, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol) along with anticoagulation therapy (low-molecular-weight heparin and rivaroxaban). Surgical intervention (debridement and drainage) was required due to abscess formation during treatment.ResultsInitially, the patient's DVT had an unclear etiology but was ultimately attributed to MTB. Despite complications including tuberculous abscess formation, combined medical and surgical management led to a successful outcome with resolution of infection and thrombosis.ConclusionsMuscular tuberculosis, though rare, should be considered in cases of unexplained DVT, particularly in patients with risk factors such as invasive procedures (eg, acupuncture). Early diagnosis, combined anti-TB therapy, anticoagulation, and surgical intervention, when necessary, can lead to favorable outcomes.

title: Global landscape and evolution of limb-salvage reconstruction with prostheses for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours: A bibliometric analysis.
abstract: PurposeTo delineate the evolution, collaborative structure, clinically relevant themes, and emerging priorities of limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction for primary malignant bone and soft tissue tumours.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from 1 January 1995 to 31 October 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection on 31 October 2025. Co-authorship, co-citation, keyword co-occurrence and burst analyses were conducted using CiteSpace 6.4.1 and VOSviewer 1.6.20.ResultsOf 2,606 retrieved records, 2,283 underwent title and abstract screening and 997 were included. Publication output increased, peaking at 84 in 2023. The United States led publication output and cumulative citations, while China ranked second by output. Keyword analyses indicated that research attention expanded from surgical strategy selection for specific tumour types and anatomical sites to include long-term prosthetic survival, complications and functional outcomes. Recent research themes included technologies such as 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and finite element analysis, with "3d printing" showing the strongest keyword burst (strength 9.49; 2021-2025). Research output was concentrated in a small number of centres and journals. Frequently co-cited publications provided standardised methods for assessing limb function and classifying endoprosthetic failure.ConclusionsLong-term prosthetic survival, complications, function and quality of life remain central themes in limb-salvage prosthetic reconstruction. Technologies supporting individualised reconstruction, including 3D printing, computer-assisted navigation and emerging robot-assisted techniques, are attracting increasing research interest. Future multicentre comparative studies should use standardised outcome measures and long-term follow-up to evaluate prosthesis design, fixation and selection, as well as strategies for preventing and managing reconstructive failure.

title: Hybrid Revascularization of Chronic Vertebral Artery Occlusion: A Morphology-Based Classification, Novel Collateral-Channel Techniques, and Mid-Term Patency in a Single-Center Series of 26 Procedures.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic vertebral artery (VA) occlusion encompasses heterogeneous morphologies-de novo atherosclerotic occlusion, in-stent restenosis (ISR), and in-stent occlusion (ISO)-for which no classification-guided revascularization strategy exists. We report the largest single-center series of hybrid revascularization combining VA endarterectomy (VEA) with endovascular techniques, propose a morphology-based classification, and provide the first mid-term patency analysis. METHODS: Twenty-six consecutive hybrid revascularization procedures performed in 25 patients with chronic VA occlusion between January 2018 and March 2026 were retrospectively analyzed. Lesions were classified as Type I (de novo occlusion), Type II (post-stent ISR), or Type III (post-stent ISO), with a complexity modifier "C" denoting long-segment extension, tortuous/deep origin, or absence of a distal target. Technical success, periprocedural complications, and patency at last imaging follow-up were assessed. RESULTS: Technical success was 88.5% (23/26) overall, declining across morphological types: 100% in Type I, 88.9% in Type II, and 71.4% in Type III. The C modifier strongly predicted failure (success 50.0% vs. 100% without C; P = 0.008). There was no periprocedural stroke or death; one major cardiac event (3.8%) occurred. At last follow-up (median 34 months; range, 3-96 months), 19 of 23 successfully recanalized arteries (82.6%) remained patent. Mid-term patency was 100% with adjunctive stenting versus 63.6% without (P = 0.037); both reocclusions and one of two restenoses followed stent explantation without re-scaffolding. Novel bailout techniques-VA transposition to the thyrocervical trunk and retrograde revascularization through the ascending cervical artery collateral-rescued three complex anatomies. CONCLUSIONS: Hybrid revascularization is safe and effective for chronic VA occlusion, with outcomes that depend systematically on lesion morphology. The proposed Type I/II/III classification with the C modifier stratifies technical difficulty and guides strategy selection, while adjunctive stent scaffolding after endarterectomy appears critical for durable patency. These hypothesis-generating findings warrant prospective validation.

title: Sirtuins in cellular senescence and cardiovascular diseases: From mechanistic basis to activator development and translational perspectives.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and cellular senescence serves as a core driving factor in the pathogenesis and progression of cardiovascular degeneration and related diseases. Sirtuins act as a crucial molecular hub linking cellular senescence to CVDs, and their upregulated activity is closely associated with delayed cellular senescence and preserved normal cardiovascular function; therefore, the research and development of small-molecule Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) hold important research value and promising translational potential for CVD intervention. This review systematically elucidates the molecular mechanisms by which various Sirtuin subtypes influence senescence-related processes in CVDs through the regulation of biological events such as DNA damage repair, mitochondrial homeostasis, oxidative stress, and inflammatory responses. Furthermore, it comprehensively outlines their roles in major cardiovascular conditions, including hypertension, angiogenesis, atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysm and dissection, and heart failure. Finally, this paper summarizes recent advances in the development of Sirtuin activators and, in light of current challenges such as insufficient specificity and hurdles in clinical translation, provides perspectives on the future development of Sirtuin-targeted therapies for the prevention and treatment of CVDs.

title: + NLRP3Macrophages: Central Inflammatory Nodes of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm and Potential Cellular Target of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acids.
abstract: + + Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a fatal inflammatory vascular disease without effective clinical treatments. Dietary patterns regulate aortic inflammation, and Mediterranean diet-derived omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFA) exert anti-inflammatory effects, yet their cellular targets in AAA remain unclear. We integrated three single-cell RNA-seq cohorts (12 AAA, 3 controls) and constructed a human aortic cell atlas with 64,258 cells. Pseudo-bulk analysis and CoVarNet multicellular network analysis revealed a core remodeling axis: protective FOLR2resident macrophages were depleted, while a unique AAA-enriched NLRP3inflammatory macrophage population (M08_Mph_NLRP3) formed the hub of pathological inflammatory networks. Three bulk transcriptomic cohorts and five complementary enrichment approaches verified this signature. An LPS/OX-LDL/IL-1β-stimulated THP-1 model recapitulated AAA macrophage pathological changes including NLRP3 inflammasome overactivation, enhanced proliferation and migration. Further functional tests demonstrated ω-3 PUFA markedly blocked inflammasome cascade, reduced IL-1β/IL-18 release and reversed all macrophage pathological phenotypes. This study identifies M08_Mph_NLRP3 as the important inflammatory mediator of AAA and provides single-cell and in vitro functional evidence supporting ω-3 PUFA as a candidate nutritional agent targeting NLRP3-driven vascular inflammation.

title: Early-onset Pulmonary Embolism After Prolonged Combined Cosmetic Breast Surgery: 2 Case Reports and a Literature Review.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures. Procedures lasted 225 and 370 minutes, respectively. Dyspnea, chest discomfort, or palpitations occurred within 48 hours postoperatively. D-dimer was elevated, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed acute PE, including a saddle embolus in 1 patient. Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin followed by rivaroxaban led to clinical improvement without observed recurrence at the short-term follow-up. A focused literature review identified additional thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast surgery, most within the first postoperative week. Early-onset PE can complicate prolonged, combined cosmetic breast surgery even in patients classified as intermediate risk. Pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis before symptom onset could not be reliably ascertained from available records. These cases support a protocolized, Caprini-informed pathway that specifies routine mechanical measures and clear indications, agent/dose, and timing for chemoprophylaxis, with explicit documentation and vigilance for early postoperative cardiopulmonary symptoms.
englishSummary: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures.

title: Pantothenate metabolic alterations in PROS1 mutation carriers and the antithrombotic effects of pantethine.
abstract: Background Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1‑mutation patients through integrated multi‑omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models. Methods Serum metabolomics, siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed. Results Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM‑1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF‑κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL‑1β‑induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM‑1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine‑conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co‑incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation‑driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet mode of interaction. Conclusions This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet association in Protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1‑deficient in vivo models.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Endovascular Treatment for Ruptured Internal Carotid Artery Pseudoaneurysms Secondary to Radiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of endovascular intervention in treating ruptured internal carotid artery (ICA) pseudoaneurysms secondary to radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed. Balloon test occlusion (BTO) was performed selectively when parent artery occlusion (PAO) was considered feasible. Treatment was individualized using covered stent implantation, coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, or PAO. Outcomes included final angiographic hemostasis, recurrent bleeding, complications (analyzed as events when patients had more than one event), and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at last follow-up. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were analyzed: 15 underwent coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, 12 covered stent implantation, and 5 PAO. BTO was performed in 8 patients (25.0%): 5 tolerated BTO and underwent PAO, whereas 3 had inadequate collateral reserve and received reconstructive treatment. Final angiographic hemostasis was achieved in all 32 patients (100%; 95% exact CI 89.1-100%). At last follow-up, 28 patients (87.5%; 95% CI 71.0%-96.5%) had mRS 0-1. Six complication events were recorded across 32 procedures (18.8 events per 100 procedures): 4 recurrent bleeding events and 2 transient limb weakness events, graded as Medical Research Council muscle-power grade 3. One patient contributed both recurrent bleeding and transient weakness; therefore event rates should not be interpreted as unique-patient incidence. No severe complications were observed. CONCLUSION: Endovascular treatment achieved immediate hemostasis in this small, retrospective series of ruptured radiation-related ICA pseudoaneurysms. Treatment should be individualized according to collateral reserve, vascular anatomy, and the feasibility of BTO. Covered stents and coil-based reconstruction can preserve the parent artery but require close surveillance for endoleak, residual pseudoaneurysm, and new lesions. PAO may be considered only when collateral circulation is adequate; the zero-event estimate in five patients has a wide confidence interval. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Development and application of evaluation criteria for venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies during the perioperative period.
abstract: i C i C BackgroundPatients with gynecologic malignancies face a high perioperative VTE risk and suboptimal prevention adherence, yet lack systematic, evidence-based evaluation standards.ObjectiveTo develop and preliminarily validate evidence-based, comprehensive evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in this population.MethodsThe Delphi method was employed to formulate the evaluation criteria for VTE prevention in this population. The Attribute Hierarchical Model (AHM) was used to assign a weight to each indicator, and the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) was applied to evaluate adherence to perioperative VTE prevention standards among patients undergoing gynecologic surgery at our hospital.ResultsThe final criteria included 12 indicators covering quantitative and dynamic VTE risk assessment, bleeding risk evaluation, implementation of basic prophylaxis, assessment of indications and contraindications for mechanical and pharmacologic prophylaxis, timing, dosing, and duration of anticoagulant prophylaxis, and monitoring of efficacy and safety. The indicator weight coefficients ranged from 0.0234 to 0.1357. Among the 107 patients, 62 (57.94%) had ≥ 0.6, and 45 (42.06%) had < 0.6. Indicator-level analysis showed 100% compliance for basic prophylaxis, mechanical prophylaxis indications, and absence of contraindications to pharmacologic prophylaxis. The lowest compliance rates were observed for quantitative VTE risk assessment (25.23%, 27/107), dynamic VTE risk assessment (32.71%, 35/107), initiation timing (24.30%, 26/107), prophylaxis duration (24.30%, 26/107), and efficacy and safety monitoring (14.95%, 16/107).ConclusionThis study developed scientifically grounded and clinically feasible evaluation criteria for perioperative VTE prevention in patients with gynecologic malignancies. They provide a practical basis for quality improvement and ongoing refinement of institutional VTE prevention strategies.

title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear. METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS). RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory. DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT. title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups. RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.

title: Preprocedural angiographic difference in cerebral circulation time and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion for middle cerebral artery occlusion.
abstract: PURPOSE: To investigate whether the affected-to-contralateral difference in cerebral circulation time (ΔCCT) on preprocedural digital subtraction angiography is associated with early neurological and 90-day functional outcomes after endovascular treatment (EVT) and successful reperfusion. METHODS: Patients with acute M1 or non-distal M2 middle cerebral artery occlusion who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion (mTICI ≥2b) were retrospectively included. Semi-automatically measured ΔCCT was evaluated in relation to the primary outcome of 24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) improvement and the exploratory outcomes of early neurological deterioration (END) and a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score ≥ 3. Models were adjusted for age, sex, baseline NIHSS score, collateral status, and occlusion location. RESULTS: Among 132 patients, the median ΔCCT was 1.31 s (IQR, 0.97-1.67 s). Each 1-standard-deviation increase in ΔCCT was associated with 3.39 points less 24-hour NIHSS improvement (adjusted β = -3.39, 95% confidence interval [CI] -4.79 to -1.98; P < 0.001), higher odds of END (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 3.11, 95% CI 1.92-5.42; P < 0.001), and higher odds of a 90-day mRS score ≥ 3 (aOR 1.58, 95% CI 1.06-2.41; P = 0.028). CONCLUSION: Among patients with M1 or non-distal M2 occlusion who achieved successful reperfusion, a longer pre-EVT ΔCCT was associated with less early neurological improvement and, in exploratory analyses, higher odds of END and an unfavorable 90-day outcome. Its generalizability to broader EVT populations requires further evaluation.

title: Quantification of vortex characteristics and rupture risk assessment in abdominal aortic aneurysms using the liutex method.
abstract: The blood flow of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) is characterized by complex vortex interactions. Previous studies have found three flow types in AAAs (Type I: multiple vortices; Type II: non-helical single vortex; Type III: helical main flow channel), and Type III has strong correlation with rupture risk. However, flow pattern classification is subjective and qualitative, hindering further improvements in risk prediction. To enhance the predictive value of vortex-based metrics, three-dimensional models of 40 infrarenal AAAs (22 ruptured and 18 unruptured) were reconstructed from preoperative CTA images for computational fluid dynamics analysis. Flow pattern types and two novel quantitative vortex parameters based on Liutex method (volume vortex fraction (vVF) and directional entropy (H)) were compared between the two groups. A multiparametric rupture risk prediction model was constructed. Receiver operating characteristic curves and the area under the curve (AUC) were employed to evaluate predictive performance. Results demonstrated that vVF in the ruptured group was significantly higher (p = 0.02). Type III AAAs exhibited a median vVF of 15.29 %, significantly surpassing those of Types I and II, and a 12.5 % threshold achieved 80 % accuracy in identifying these high-risk patterns. Ruptured cases exhibited higher entropy, facilitating more granular risk stratification. Ultimately, the integrated model combining maximum diameter, flow pattern, and directional entropy achieved an AUC of 0.86 (p < 0.001). By objectively quantifying vortex structures and establishing a multiparametric prediction model, this study significantly enhances the predictive accuracy for AAA rupture, providing a reference for risk evaluation.

title: Association of Advanced Age With Functional Recovery After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large-core Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Evidence supporting endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large-core ischemic stroke has expanded, but outcomes in patients aged ≥80 years remain insufficiently characterized. We evaluated outcomes after EVT in this population, with particular attention to prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with anterior-circulation large vessel occlusion and large-core stroke (Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score 0 to 5 or CT perfusion core volume ≥50 mL) treated with EVT between October 2019 and September 2025. The primary outcome was prestroke disability-adjusted functional recovery, defined as 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) ≤ prestroke mRS + 1. RESULTS: Among 377 patients, 75 were aged ≥80 years, and 302 were <80 years. Functional recovery occurred in 14.7% and 18.9%, respectively. Age ≥80 years was not significantly associated with functional recovery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.00; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.45-2.22; p = 0.992). Patients aged ≥80 years had lower odds of mRS 0 to 3 (aOR, 0.41; 95% CI, 0.21-0.79) and higher odds of mortality (aOR, 1.79; 95% CI, 1.01-3.16). Successful reperfusion and hemorrhagic outcomes did not differ significantly between groups. Each 10-year increase in age was associated with lower odds of functional recovery (aOR, 0.60; 95% CI, 0.46-0.77). CONCLUSION: Among selected patients aged ≥80 years with large-core ischemic stroke, successful reperfusion and functional recovery remained achievable after EVT, despite poorer conventional functional outcomes and higher mortality. Advancing age was associated with progressively worse outcomes when modeled continuously. These findings support individualized prognostic assessment after EVT rather than reliance on chronological age alone.

title: The pathological role of chemokines and chemokine receptors in diabetic vascular disease.
abstract: Diabetic vascular diseases, which include microvascular and macrovascular diseases, are a common complication of diabetes mellitus. Both chemokines and their receptors are involved in the pathophysiological process of diabetic vascular diseases, given their diverse functions. Crucially, when evaluating these chemokine networks, it is essential to distinguish descriptive clinical and bioinformatic biomarker observations from functional causal mechanisms established through in vitro and in vivo interventional studies, as observational concentration changes alone do not inherently demonstrate a direct pathogenic role or identify a therapeutic target. In this review, we examine recent studies and provide an overview of the mechanisms underlying chemokine-mediated signaling in diabetic microvascular and macrovascular diseases. We conclude that while circulating chemokines primarily serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers, specific functional chemokine axes represent viable therapeutic targets for diabetic vascular complications.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
abstract: In vitro Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers., small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis.

title: Ischemic electrocardiographic changes and initial misdiagnosis of acute aortic syndromes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Ischemic electrocardiographic (ECG) changes can mimic acute myocardial infarction and obscure acute aortic dissection (AAD) or other acute aortic syndromes (AAS), but their association with initial misdiagnosis has not been synthesized. We assessed whether ischemic changes on the earliest prediagnostic ECG were associated with initial misdiagnosis. METHODS: We searched PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and the China National Knowledge Infrastructure through July 1, 2026, for observational studies of confirmed AAD/AAS reporting 2 × 2 data for initial misdiagnosis by ischemic ECG status. Unadjusted odds ratios (ORs) were pooled with a random-effects model using restricted maximum-likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity, prediction intervals, leave-one-out sensitivity, QUIPS risk of bias, and GRADE certainty were assessed. RESULTS: 2 Seven retrospective cohorts from four countries included 724 cases; 609 had analyzable ECG data, including 179 initial misdiagnoses. Ischemic ECG changes were not significantly associated with initial misdiagnosis (pooled unadjusted OR, 1.419; 95% CI, 0.608-3.312; P = 0.351; 95% prediction interval, 0.223-9.039; I = 62.9%). All leave-one-out 95% CIs included 1.0. Excluding the principal contributor to heterogeneity yielded an OR of 1.050 (95% CI, 0.591-1.865) with negligible residual heterogeneity. No QUIPS domain was at high risk; GRADE certainty was moderate after downgrading for serious imprecision. CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence did not demonstrate a significant association, but wide confidence and prediction intervals and unadjusted retrospective data leave important effects unresolved. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized ECG timing, harmonized diagnostic criteria, and multivariable adjustment are needed.

title: Case Report: Suspected Lower Limb Congestive Injury Associated with Decreased Compliance of the External Iliac Vein After Laparoscopic Myomectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incidence of lower extremity deep vein thrombosis following gynecologic laparoscopy is 4.0%, whereas postoperative well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) is much rarer, with a reported incidence of only 0.03%-0.20%. Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature. CASE PRESENTATION: A 44-year-old woman underwent an 8-hour gynecologic laparoscopic procedure in the Lloyd-Davies position. Thirty minutes after surgery, she developed acute swelling, pain, and numbness of the right lower limb. Deep vein thrombosis was initially suspected, but treatment was ineffective. Unilateral well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) was subsequently considered, and her symptoms were relieved following supportive treatment, including dehydration therapy and elevation of the affected limb. Repeated review of the surgical video suggested lower limb congestive injury potentially associated with decreased compliance of the external iliac vein. The patient also experienced persistent postoperative symptoms resembling venous intermittent claudication, consistent with the clinical manifestations of impaired external iliac venous outflow. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the need for increased attention to the condition of the external iliac vascular sheath during gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Swelling and thickening of the vascular sheath, resulting in decreased compliance of the venous wall, may lead to severe venous congestion injury of the lower limb and may require timely intraoperative intervention when necessary. This case may provide a reference for the clinical diagnosis and management of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain following gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.

We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT. METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049). CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT.

title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm. RESULTS: A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%). CONCLUSION: This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD. METHODS: In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA). RESULTS: Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow. CONCLUSIONS: Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

title: Untargeted Plasma Metabolomics Reveals Molecular Subtypes Associated with Reintervention Risk in Peripheral Artery Disease after Revascularization.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity after revascularization that is incompletely explained by conventional severity indicators. We performed untargeted plasma LC-MS metabolomics in 175 PAD patients undergoing revascularization and applied variability-based feature selection, unsupervised clustering, pathway and chemical-class analyses, survival modeling, and metabolite prioritization. Three metabolically defined molecular subtypes were identified: redox protective (n = 93), metabolic burden (n = 72), and renal dysfunction (n = 10). Compared to the redox-protective subtype, the metabolic-burden subtype showed higher risks of composite adverse outcomes, reintervention, and major adverse cardiovascular events, accompanied by acylcarnitine accumulation, fatty-acyl enrichment, and COX-prostaglandin-related inflammatory signaling. Secondary clustering of high-risk patients identified a subgroup with increased reintervention risk, despite no corresponding increase in Rutherford classification or ankle-brachial index severity, characterized by sphingomyelin, diglyceride, and thromboxane/leukotriene-related lipid mediator signatures. A five-metabolite score was associated with reintervention risk and showed numerically higher apparent discrimination than the original and expanded clinical models. These findings establish an untargeted metabolomics framework for molecular subtyping of PAD after revascularization and nominate metabolic phenotypes for future validation.

title: Personalized anticoagulation and drug monitoring for pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism in hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency.
abstract: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare. The principal therapeutic challenge lies in the absence of established guidelines regarding optimal anticoagulant selection, dosing strategies, and monitoring approaches for such patients, contributing to treatment failure in her first four pregnancies. The patient was referred to our institution before her fifth conception. Preconception intervention began, and we instituted low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) therapy, with dose titration guided by thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT) and anti-Xa activity levels. This regimen demonstrated safety and efficacy, achieving a maximum nadroparin dose of 10 250 IU twice daily. Under close pharmacotherapeutic monitoring by a clinical pharmacist using this individualized protocol, the patient achieved a successful term delivery and was discharged.
englishSummary: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare.

title: Perioperative combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid does not increase venous thromboembolism risk after total knee arthroplasty in plateau areas: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: After total knee arthroplasty (TKA), rivaroxaban is often used to prevent venous thromboembolism (VTE), while tranexamic acid (TXA) is used to reduce perioperative bleeding. However, plateau hypoxia may affect coagulation. We assessed whether combined intravenous and intra-articular TXA increases VTE risk in plateau TKA patients. This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, pilot controlled trial was conducted at altitude greater than 3500 m. Fifty unilateral TKA patients were randomized to experimental (intravenous + intra-articular TXA) or control (intravenous TXA alone). All received rivaroxaban for 14 days. Primary outcome was new-onset DVT (deep vein thrombosis) or PE (Pulmonary Embolism) at day 3; secondary outcomes included thromboelastography (TEG) and coagulation parameters at 6 h, 1, 2, and 3 days. No VTE occurred in either group. Nonthrombotic ultrasound findings (intermuscular vein dilation with blood stasis) were observed in 9/25 (36%) of the experimental group and 13/25 (52%) of the control group, with no between-group difference (P = 0.254). TEG parameters showed no significant differences, except for a transiently lower D-dimer in the experimental group on day 1 (P < 0.001), though clinical relevance is unclear. Hb and Hct declined less in the experimental group at all time points (P < 0.05), suggesting reduced blood loss. In plateau TKA patients, adding intra-articular TXA to intravenous TXA did not increase short-term VTE risk. These preliminary findings suggest combined TXA with rivaroxaban may be well tolerated in this population.

title: Combined antegrade-retrograde technique in urgent carotid stenting for true lumen compression after total arch replacement.
abstract: Type A aortic dissection extending into the carotid arteries with true lumen compression poses a significant risk of cerebral hypoperfusion and neurological sequelae. This case report describes an elderly patient who developed an extension of the right common carotid artery dissection with associated true lumen compression immediately following total arch replacement for acute Type A aortic dissection. Urgent carotid stenting was performed using a combined antegrade-retrograde approach (trans carotid and trans radial approach) to restore blood flow. Postprocedural imaging confirmed patency without major complications. This technique highlights a viable salvage strategy for managing complex aortic dissections when traditional methods fail. A literature review discusses the combined antegrade-retrograde approach used in urgent carotid stenting, as well as the advantages of ultrasound in selecting the true lumen and its minimally invasive nature.

title: Hybrid Occipital Artery-AICA Bypass Followed by Endovascular Embolization for a Radiation-Induced Dissecting AICA Aneurysm in a Pediatric Patient.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND IMPORTANCE: Pediatric anterior inferior cerebellar artery (AICA) aneurysms are rare; radiation-associated dissecting lesions require exclusion without compromising brainstem or cerebellar perforators. CLINICAL PRESENTATION: A 13-year-old boy developed a progressively enlarging right AICA a2 dissecting aneurysm after cranial irradiation for pineal nongerminomatous germ cell tumor. Because direct clipping or isolated parent vessel occlusion was considered high risk, he underwent occipital artery-AICA a3 bypass followed by endovascular coil embolization in a single hybrid session. Dual arterial access enabled transradial vertebral artery treatment and transfemoral angiographic bypass assessment. Postoperative MRI showed a small transient cerebellar ischemic lesion that resolved within 2 weeks. At 2 months, the patient was neurologically intact with patent bypass and no aneurysm recurrence. CONCLUSION: Hybrid occipital artery-AICA bypass followed by endovascular embolization is a feasible flow-preserving option for selected pediatric AICA aneurysms requiring distal perfusion preservation.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Rivaroxaban versus LMWH Thromboprophylaxis Following Gynecologic Cancer Surgery: A Retrospective Comparison Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: We aimed to evaluate the clinical outcomes of rivaroxaban vs low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) for thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic cancer surgery. PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality. A multivariable logistic regression model was used to adjust for potential confounding factors. RESULTS: A total of 250 women were included, 134 received rivaroxaban and 116 received LMWH for postoperative thromboprophylaxis following gynecologic malignancy-related surgery. After adjusting for potential confounding factors using multivariable logistic regression, the 30-day VTE and bleeding events showed no significant differences between the rivaroxaban group and the LMWH groups. There were no cases of 30-day readmission related to surgery, no 30-day mortality, and no all-cause mortality during the 1-year follow-up. Notably, all distal DVT events in both groups were calf muscular vein thromboses. During the 1-year follow-up, no patients were rehospitalized or died due to VTE. CONCLUSION: We observed no significant differences in short- and long-term outcomes between rivaroxaban and LMWH after gynecologic malignancy surgery. Given the retrospective design and limited number of events, these results should be interpreted with caution, and prospective randomized studies are warranted.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective comparative study of rivaroxaban vs standard LMWH in patients undergoing gynecologic malignancy surgery. Clinical outcomes included venous thromboembolism (VTE), major bleeding, non-major bleeding, and 1-year all-cause mortality.

title: Pulmonary Artery Interventional Thrombectomy Stent System: Combined Application of Stent and Negative Pressure Aspiration.
abstract: This protocol describes a pulmonary artery thrombectomy technique that combines stent deployment and negative pressure aspiration to achieve rapid thrombus removal and restore pulmonary arterial perfusion. Prolonged obstruction may lead to right heart dysfunction and hemodynamic instability. The pulmonary artery thrombectomy stent system provides a rapid approach to thrombus removal and restoration of pulmonary perfusion, thereby alleviating respiratory distress and hypoxemia while reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and right ventricular strain. This technique is applicable for patients with intermediate- to high-risk pulmonary embolism, particularly those with contraindications to thrombolysis. Preoperative computed tomography imaging revealed pulmonary artery emboli involving both the left and right pulmonary arteries and their branches. Following thrombectomy using the pulmonary artery interventional thrombectomy stent system, postoperative imaging confirmed complete clearance of the thrombi and full restoration of pulmonary artery blood flow.

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.
