title: Staphylococcus aureus -associated infected subclavian artery pseudoaneurysm treated with dual bare-metal stent implantation: a case report.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus Infected subclavian artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, life-threatening vascular lesions associated with high risks of rupture and mortality. We report a 70-year-old male presenting with intermittent hemoptysis, who was diagnosed with a pseudoaneurysm of the left subclavian artery adjacent to the dominant vertebral artery. Blood cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitiveinfection. The patient underwent endovascular repair with dual bare-metal stents to preserve vertebral artery perfusion. Hemoptysis completely resolved post-intervention. Complete thrombosis and occlusion of the aneurysm sac were achieved at the 3-month follow-up, with remarkable sac shrinkage observed at 6 months. This case suggests that dual bare-metal stents may represent a feasible potential treatment alternative for highly selected patients with infected subclavian artery aneurysms. Long-term safety and efficacy remain to be further verified. Long-term antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance remain mandatory.

title: Quality and reliability of short videos about type A aortic dissection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the quality and reliability of TAAD-related short videos on TikTok and Bilibili, with particular attention to platform differences and uploader characteristics. METHODS: The top 250 videos ranked by comprehensive ranking on each platform were screened using the Chinese keyword "A." A total of 391 eligible videos were included. Uploaders were classified as medical practitioners, individual users, or institutions. Video quality and reliability were assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmarks, and Video Information Quality Instrument (VIQI). Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with video quality. RESULTS: TikTok videos showed higher engagement, whereas Bilibili videos were longer and provided broader coverage of epidemiology, etiology, and clinical presentation-related content. TikTok remained independently associated with higher VIQI scores after adjustment. Medical practitioners and institutions generally achieved higher VIQI and JAMA scores than individual users, and content coverage score was independently associated with higher video quality. However, mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly among uploader types. CONCLUSION: TAAD-related short videos demonstrated moderate overall quality but limited reliability. Platform characteristics, uploader type, and content coverage were associated with assessed information quality. Professional participation may improve some aspects of health communication, but uploader identity alone does not ensure higher reliability or transparency.

title: Yeast Mitochondrial Escape 1-Like as a Mitochondrial Gatekeeper in Aging-Related Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of aging and is closely linked to the progression of cardiovascular disease. Yeast mitochondrial escape 1-like (YME1L) is an adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent i-AAA (intermembrane space AAA, AAA=ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protease embedded in the mitochondrial inner membrane that maintains mitochondrial homeostasis by regulating proteostasis, cristae architecture, and metabolic adaptation. Notably, YME1L influences mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics, respiratory chain supercomplex organization, and oxidative phosphorylation efficiency through the regulated processing of optic atrophy protein 1 (OPA1). Accumulating evidence suggests that age-associated impairment of YME1L function contributes to mitochondrial fragmentation, energetic insufficiency, and reduced stress tolerance, particularly in long-lived, high-energy demand tissues. In the cardiovascular system, experimental models indicate that YME1L deficiency disrupts cristae organization, promotes maladaptive metabolic remodeling, and promotes heart failure-like phenotypes. Conversely, preservation of YME1L activity supports mitochondrial integrity and enhances cardiac resilience under hemodynamic stress. In addition to cardiomyocytes, YME1L also supports endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby linking mitochondrial proteostasis to vascular aging and diastolic dysfunction. Although YME1L has been extensively studied in cancer biology, its relevance to aging-related cardiovascular vulnerability is increasingly recognized, especially in cardio-oncology, where therapy-induced mitochondrial stress may be exacerbated by age-dependent decline in mitochondrial quality control. This review integrates current evidence supporting YME1L as a context-dependent regulator of mitochondrial stress adaptation, with particular emphasis on the roles of YME1L in cardiovascular aging, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and stress tolerance. Rather than positioning YME1L as a universal therapeutic target, we discuss how modulating YME1L-associated pathways may help preserve mitochondrial resilience and mitigate age-related cardiovascular dysfunction.

title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis. RESULTS: n P P P Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022. In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort ( = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2). CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Traditional Chinese medicine for diabetic lower extremity arterial disease: A review of recent advances.
abstract: Diabetic lower-extremity arterial disease (LEAD) is a prevalent macrovascular complication of diabetes and a critical pathological foundation for diabetic foot lesions. Its pathogenesis involves glycolipid metabolic disturbance, excessive oxidative stress, persistent vascular inflammation, and endothelial dysfunction, leading to limb ischemia, refractory foot ulcers, and increased amputation risk. Current standard treatments, including glycemic and lipid control, antiplatelet therapy, and endovascular revascularization, have improved clinical outcomes but still face challenges in fully ameliorating microcirculatory impairment and preventing long-term restenosis. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts multi-component and multi-target protective effects against diabetic LEAD. This review summarizes pharmacological advances in representative TCM agents, including Salvia miltiorrhiza, Astragali Radix, and their bioactive constituents (e.g., tanshinone IIA sulfonate, salvianolic acid B, astragaloside IV, and Astragalus polysaccharide), as well as classical formulas and patent medicines such as Huangqi Guizhi Wuwu Decoction, Tongxinluo capsule, Tangbi capsule, and Danggui Sini Decoction. Their mechanisms involve protecting vascular endothelium, regulating glycolipid metabolism, suppressing vascular inflammation via NF-κB and NLRP3 pathways, and activating Nrf2-mediated antioxidant defense, HIF-1α/VEGF, PI3K-AKT, and Ang-1/Tie-2 signaling to restore microcirculation and promote angiogenesis. Clinically, TCM-assisted endovascular intervention reduces postoperative restenosis and improves lower-limb perfusion; external preparations promote diabetic foot ulcer healing; acupuncture, moxibustion, and mind-body exercises improve microcirculation and long-term management. TCM is a promising adjunctive strategy for diabetic LEAD, and further mechanistic and clinical studies are needed to advance its standardized application and improve patient prognosis.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: N I p 2 Eleven studies (total = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( = 29.0%, = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

title: Clinical significance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index in glycemic control and ischemic limb damage in type 2 diabetes with chronic limb-threatening ischemia.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the clinical relevance of the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) complicated by chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) . METHODS: A total of 520 patients with CLTI were collected and divided into two groups based on the history of T2DM: the combined T2DM group and the non-T2DM group. The CTI of the patients was calculated, and its relationship with blood glucose control levels, risk factors, and the degree of ischemia in CLTI patients was analyzed. RESULTS: P P P P P The CTI in the combined T2DM group was significantly greater than that in the non-T2DM group ( < 0.001). The CTI in the poorly controlled blood glucose group was significantly greater than that in the well controlled blood glucose group ( < 0.001). Regardless of whether CLTI patients had T2DM, the CTI in the overweight group was greater than that in the non-overweight group ( < 0.05). The area under the curve (AUC) for the CTI discriminating the high wound, ischemia, and foot infection (WIfI) classification was 0.813 ( < 0.001). Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses showed that an increased CTI was an independently associated factor for the high WIfI classification in CLTI patients (OR = 6.409, < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that patients with CLTI and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels. CONCLUSIONS: The CTI was closely related to the presence of T2DM, blood glucose control level, and overweight status in CLTI patients. The CTI has certain clinical value in discriminating the degree of ischemia in CLTI, and high CTI levels had significantly lower 1-year amputation-free survival compared to those with low CTI levels.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Predicting Amputation and Related Outcomes in Peripheral Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) affects over 236 million individuals globally and carries substantial risks of amputation, major adverse limb events, and mortality. Existing clinical scoring systems focus on short-term surgical outcomes and lack generalizability. Machine learning (ML) has emerged as a promising tool for PAD outcome prediction. We aimed to conduct the first quantitative meta-analysis evaluation the discriminative performance, methodological rigor, and certainty of evidence of ML-based prognostic models for adverse limb outcomes in PAD. METHODS: Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)/Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses literature search extension (PRISMA-S) guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception through March 15, 2026. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and Prediction model Risk Of Bias Assessment Tool risk-of-bias assessment. Random-effects meta-analysis (DerSimonian-Laird with Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman correction) and hierarchical summary receiver operating characteristic (HSROC) analysis were performed; certainty was rated with Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation (GRADE). RESULTS: 2 Ten studies were included. The pooled area under the curve (AUC) for amputation-related outcomes was 0.88 (95% confidence interval, 0.83-0.94; prediction interval, 0.79-0.98) with substantial heterogeneity (I= 95.4%). HSROC yielded pooled sensitivity 0.85 and specificity 0.84. Registry-based studies showed higher pooled AUC than nonregistry studies (0.92 vs 0.80; P = 0.004). All models had a high or unclear risk of bias in the analysis domain; none underwent independent external validation. GRADE certainty was very low. CONCLUSION: ML models demonstrate high discriminative performance for predicting amputation-related outcomes in PAD, but very low certainty of evidence, absence of external validation, and high risk of bias currently limit clinical implementation. Prospective multicenter validation and adherence to artificial intelligence reporting guidelines are essential before clinical translation.

title: Association between Increased Superficial Calcification Clusters in Carotid Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Events after Carotid Artery Stenting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on computed tomography angiography. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P = 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P = 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P = 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P = 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P = 0.0256, HR = 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P = 0.0265, HR = 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

title: Proton pump inhibitor use was not associated with reduced gastrointestinal bleeding risk in ischemic stroke patients treated with dual antiplatelet therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate the association between proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use and gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS) patients receiving dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 3,122 AIS patients with large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) treated with DAPT at Qingdao University Affiliated Hospital (September 2020-December 2023). Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics. To address confounding by indication, we additionally performed 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM) as a sensitivity analysis, with conditional logistic regression applied to the matched cohort. RESULTS: 45.0% (n = 1,404) received concomitant PPI. No significant difference in GIB incidence was observed between PPI users and non-PPI users (2.1% vs. 1.3%, p = 0.12). Subgroup analyses revealed that PPI use was significantly associated with increased GIB risk in non-endovascular therapy patients (aOR = 2.08, p = 0.03), particularly those with posterior circulation infarction (aOR = 5.96, p = 0.006). These findings were further supported by propensity score matching analysis (conditional OR = 1.64, 95% CI 0.87-3.09, p = 0.124 for the overall cohort; conditional OR = 12.29, 95% CI 1.59-94.90, p = 0.016 for posterior circulation infarction in the non-endovascular subgroup). No significant association between PPI use and GIB risk was found in endovascular therapy or age-stratified subgroups. CONCLUSION: PPI use was not associated with reduced overall GIB risk in DAPT-treated AIS patients. Routine PPI prophylaxis may be unnecessary for low-bleeding-risk populations, while the association observed in posterior circulation infarction remains hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation.

Adjusted odds ratios (aORs) for GIB were calculated using binary logistic regression, controlling for confounders including age, sex, and other baseline characteristics.

title: Chocolate Balloon Versus Conventional Balloon for Vessel Preparation Before Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Lesions: A Real-World Propensity Score-Matched Study.
abstract: To evaluate the procedural and 1-year clinical outcomes of the Chocolate balloon versus conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) for vessel preparation before drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment of femoropopliteal lesions. This retrospective subgroup analysis of the multicenter PROMISING registry included patients with femoropopliteal lesions treated with DCB. Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty. After 1:1 PSM, 254 patients were included in each group. The primary endpoint was bailout stenting. Secondary endpoints included maximum DCB diameter, stent length, postprocedural ankle-brachial index (ABI), 1-year clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), major amputation, all-cause mortality, amputation-free survival (AFS), and major adverse events (MAE). After PSM, bailout stenting occurred less frequently in the Chocolate balloon group than in the POBA group (20.47% vs 29.92%, p = 0.014). The Chocolate balloon group also showed a trend toward shorter stent length (20.67 ± 9.75 cm vs 23.71 ± 10.62 cm, p = 0.097) and allowed use of larger DCBs (4.96 ± 0.52 mm vs 4.74 ± 0.61 mm, p < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression identified Chocolate balloon use as an independent protective factor against bailout stenting, whereas chronic total occlusion and severe calcification were independent predictors of bailout stenting. No significant differences were observed in 1-year clinical outcomes. Compared with POBA, Chocolate balloon vessel preparation reduced bailout stenting and enabled use of larger DCBs, suggesting potential procedural advantages in complex femoropopliteal lesions. However, these procedural benefits did not translate into improved 1-year clinical outcomes.

Before propensity score matching (PSM), 817 patients underwent POBA and 379 underwent Chocolate balloon angioplasty.

title: Incremental prognostic and risk-stratification value of ultrasound-based Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) classification for recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The Carotid Plaque Reporting and Data System (Plaque-RADS) is a system for stroke risk assessment. However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis. METHODS: Between January 2020 and December 2022, 231 patients with carotid plaque ipsilateral to the prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis were retrospectively screened, of whom 158 were included in the final analysis. US-based Plaque-RADS classification was assigned based on duplex US assessment of plaque features. Cox regression and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories and recurrent ischemic stroke. Model discrimination was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves and area under the curve (AUC), and clinical utility was evaluated using decision curve analysis. The association between increasing US-based Plaque-RADS categories and the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke was assessed by trend analysis. The incremental risk-stratification value of refined high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds was quantified with net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI). Internal validation was performed using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: vs. During the 3-year follow-up period, recurrent ischemic stroke occurred in 33 patients. High-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, after adjusting for smoking, homocysteine, and intraplaque neovascularization [adjusted hazard ratio: 3.56; 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-11.83, P=0.038]. No statistically significant interactions were observed across the subgroups (all P for interaction >0.05). The Plaque-RADS ≥3 model demonstrated a higher AUC than the conventional US model [0.816 (95% CI: 0.731-0.901)0.810 (95% CI: 0.720-0.899)] and provided a slight net benefit across selected threshold probabilities. Additionally, the risk of recurrent ischemic stroke increased with higher Plaque-RADS categories (P for trend <0.001). Among the models using different high-risk Plaque-RADS thresholds, the Plaque-RADS ≥3b model showed the best predictive performance (0.865, 95% CI: 0.799-0.930), compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model and the Plaque-RADS ≥3c model [0.824 (95% CI: 0.740-0.906)]. The Plaque-RADS ≥3b model also showed moderate improvements in NRI [0.250; (95% CI: 0.088-0.557), P=0.017] and IDI [0.090; (95% CI: 0.000-0.185), P=0.049], compared with the Plaque-RADS ≥3 model. Bootstrap internal validation indicated limited optimism across all models. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis, high-risk US-based Plaque-RADS categories were significantly associated with recurrent ischemic stroke. The US-based Plaque-RADS may help identify plaque phenotypes associated with an increased risk of recurrent ipsilateral ischemic stroke, while refined high-risk thresholds, particularly Plaque-RADS ≥3b, may provide additional value for risk stratification.

However, the clinical utility of ultrasound (US)-based Plaque-RADS remains unclear. This study aimed to assess the incremental prognostic value and risk stratification utility of US-based Plaque-RADS in patients with prior stroke and low-to-moderate-grade carotid stenosis.

title: Time-zero multimodal risk stratification for in-hospital mortality in acute aortic dissection: two-centre development, temporal and external validation, and occult shock phenotyping.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) requires rapid anatomical diagnosis and early risk stratification, yet initial blood pressure alone may miss patients with concealed hypoperfusion. Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. We aimed to develop and validate an initial 2-hour multimodal model integrating clinical, CTA, and TTE data to predict in-hospital mortality and to describe occult shock in normotensive AAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective two-centre cohort study included 2,584 adults with first-time AAD who completed CTA and TTE during the initial 2-hour assessment after emergency department triage. Cohorts were development (n=1,678; 2007-2017), internal temporal validation (n=452; 2018-2021), and external geographic/later-era validation (n=454; 2022-March 2024). Candidate variables were restricted to information available during this initial assessment window. Four supervised algorithms were compared, with ablation analyses assessing modality-specific contribution. RESULTS: XGBoost achieved optimism-corrected development area under the curve (AUC) of 0.86 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.82-0.88], internal validation 0.83 (0.79-0.87), and external validation 0.78 (0.74-0.82). Adding TTE to Clinical + CTA improved discrimination (Delta AUC +0.04, P=0.002) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) (+0.021, P=0.01). Normotensive occult shock occurred in 548/2,082 patients (26.3%) and was associated with mortality 15.9% versus 6.7% in metabolically stable normotension. CONCLUSIONS: In high-volume aortic centres where CTA and early TTE are routinely available, this initial 2-hour multimodal model showed temporal validation and moderate external discrimination for in-hospital mortality. TTE added prognostic information, particularly for type A disease, and normotensive hyperlactatemia identified a higher-risk subgroup; however, general use, type B performance, local recalibration, and action thresholds require prospective multicentre validation before clinical implementation.

Although computed tomography angiography (CTA) defines dissection anatomy and transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) provides bedside haemodynamic information, the incremental prognostic value of early TTE and the significance of normotensive hyperlactatemia remain uncertain. title: Impact of different follow-up methods on prognosis of diabetic foot patients after endovascular treatment: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) is a severe complication of diabetes mellitus, and endovascular treatment (EVT) has become the primary revascularization strategy. However, the impact of different post-procedure follow-up methods on clinical outcomes remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the effects of seven different follow-up approaches on prognosis in DFU patients after EVT. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at three tertiary hospitals in China between June 2022 and June 2025. A total of 868 DFU patients who underwent successful EVT were enrolled and categorized into seven groups based on their primary follow-up method. The primary outcomes were 12-month wound healing rate and amputation-free survival (AFS). Secondary outcomes included major adverse limb events (MALE), reintervention rate, patient satisfaction, and glycemic control. Multivariable Cox regression and propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounders. RESULTS: Among 868 patients, the surgical hospital outpatient group demonstrated the highest 12-month wound healing rate (75.0%) and AFS rate (80.1%). The no follow-up group had the poorest outcomes (45.2% wound healing, 56.4% AFS). No follow-up was associated with significantly increased risk of MALE [adjusted hazard ratio (aHR) 2.15, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.62-2.85]. WeChat follow-up (aHR 1.22, 95% CI: 0.88-1.69) showed non-significant differences compared with surgical hospital outpatient follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: Structured follow-up significantly improves wound healing and AFS in DFU patients after EVT. Digital health tools such as WeChat showed no statistically significant difference compared with traditional follow-up, but these observational data should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent effectiveness. The absence of follow-up is associated with substantially worse outcomes. These findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant validation in prospective randomized trials.

title: Association between age and in-hospital mortality and arch repair strategy in acute type A aortic dissection: a dose-response analysis of a retrospective cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Advanced age is a recognized risk factor in acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but its dose-response relationship with in-hospital mortality and the optimal extent of arch repair in elderly patients remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to determine the age-mortality dose-response relationship and to assess arch repair strategies in elderly ATAAD patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. The association between age (as a continuous variable) and in-hospital mortality was assessed using multivariable logistic regression and restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis. In a subgroup of elderly patients (≥60 years, n=115), perioperative outcomes between no/partial arch replacement and total arch replacement were compared after 1:1 propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. RESULTS: vs. Among 1,042 included patients, overall in-hospital mortality was 3.7% (39/1,042), and median age was 51 (interquartile range, 40-59) years. Age was independently associated with mortality (adjusted odds ratio 1.04 per year, 95% confidence interval: 1.01-1.07, P=0.01), and RCS analysis demonstrated a significant linear association without evidence of a threshold effect (P overall =0.02; P for non-linearity =0.31). In the elderly subgroup (n=244), 115 patients met imaging eligibility criteria for PSM, yielding 30 matched pairs. In this small matched cohort, total arch replacement was associated with longer cardiopulmonary bypass and cross-clamp times, with no statistically significant differences in mortality (6.7%3.3%) or major complications. CONCLUSIONS: Age shows a continuous linear association with in-hospital mortality after ATAAD repair, without evidence of a threshold effect. In elderly patients, total arch replacement and limited arch repair showed no statistically significant differences in early outcomes in this small matched cohort, suggesting that operative strategy should be individualized based on anatomical and physiological risk rather than age alone-a finding that warrants validation in larger studies.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive ATAAD patients who underwent surgical repair at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024.

title: Incidence and Predictors of Complications After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to VARC-3 Criteria: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite continuous advancements in devices and techniques, transcatheter aortic valve implantation remains associated with complications impacting outcomes. In 2021, the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC) introduced the VARC-3 criteria to better classify procedural complications. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting transcatheter aortic valve implantation-related complications using VARC-3 definitions between 2021 and 2025. The primary end point was all-cause mortality at latest follow-up. Secondary end points included major VARC-3 complications and predictors of adverse events. RESULTS: A total of 57 studies with 73 588 patients were included. The cohort had a mean age of 81.7 years, 51.7% were women, and most had preserved ejection fraction (55.5%) and low-to-moderate surgical risk (Society of Thoracic Surgeons [STS] predicted risk of mortality [PROM] 4.1%). Technical and 30-day device success rates were 95% and 90%, respectively; early safety rate at 30 days was 66%. At average 12 months follow-up, all-cause mortality was 10.2%. The most common complication was permanent pacemaker implantation (13%), followed by type 2 or greater bleeding (9.7%), acute kidney injury stage 3-4 (4.7%), major vascular events (4.3%), and stroke (3.0%). Moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation and patient-prosthesis mismatch occurred in 4% and 8%, respectively. Study-level pooled predictor analyses showed that acute kidney injury, type 2 or greater bleeding, paravalvular regurgitation, non-structural valve dysfunction, and higher STS score were associated with higher mortality, while eccentric/severe aortic valve calcification was associated with significant paravalvular regurgitation. CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation shows high procedural success but non-negligible complication rates under VARC-3 criteria. acute kidney injury, type 2 or greater bleeding, NSVD, periprocedural stroke and myocardial infarction after transcatheter aortic valve implantation were associated with higher mortality.

In 2021, the Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC) introduced the VARC-3 criteria to better classify procedural complications. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies reporting transcatheter aortic valve implantation-related complications using VARC-3 definitions between 2021 and 2025.

title: Computed Tomography-Based Periaortic Adipose Tissue Imaging Phenotypes in Type B Aortic Dissection: A Retrospective Case-Control Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The periaortic microenvironment visible on routine computed tomography angiography remains incompletely characterized in type B aortic dissection (TBAD). We evaluated computed tomography angiography-based periaortic adipose tissue (PAAT) phenotypes associated with prevalent TBAD and explored a prespecified Tear Risk Index for post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair aortic dilation. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 100 patients with TBAD undergoing primary thoracic endovascular aortic repair and 50 normal controls frequency matched by age and sex. Deep learning-assisted, radiologist-reviewed segmentation quantified multilayer PAAT and aortic morphology. Interreader reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analyses. Group comparisons, receiver operating characteristic analyses, and adjusted logistic regression were performed. RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with TBAD had larger aortic volume and higher 3-mm PAAT volume, fat attenuation index, and fragmentation index. Aortic volume showed an area under the curve of 0.966 (95% CI, 0.941-0.991); corresponding values for 3-mm PAAT volume, fat attenuation index, and fragmentation index were 0.614, 0.819, and 0.716, respectively. Interreader intraclass correlation coefficients for selected 3-mm PAAT measures ranged from 0.822 to 0.907. Principal TBAD-control PAAT findings remained supported after false discovery rate correction, whereas post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair PAAT differences were not robust. Tear Risk Index showed limited exploratory discrimination for dilation status. CONCLUSIONS: Selected 3-mm PAAT measures characterize a reproducible computed tomography angiography-based imaging phenotype associated with prevalent TBAD and may complement conventional aortic morphology. These findings are hypothesis generating, and Tear Risk Index should not be used as a standalone clinical predictor.

We evaluated computed tomography angiography-based periaortic adipose tissue (PAAT) phenotypes associated with prevalent TBAD and explored a prespecified Tear Risk Index for post-thoracic endovascular aortic repair aortic dilation. METHODS: This retrospective case-control study included 100 patients with TBAD undergoing primary thoracic endovascular aortic repair and 50 normal controls frequency matched by age and sex.

title: Development and external validation of risk prediction models for gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic dissection surgery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) following surgery for aortic dissection (AD) is a life-threatening complication associated with elevated mortality and increased healthcare resource utilization. However, reliable predictive tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database. METHODS: Patients who underwent AD surgery were identified from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database (MIMIC-IV; development cohort) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD; external evaluation cohort). The primary outcome was postoperative GIB within 30 days, defined using a composite database-derived algorithm requiring either (I) a hemoglobin (Hb) decrease of ≥2 g/dL accompanied by at least one supporting indicator, including a transfusion record, hemostatic medication use, or endoscopic examination; or (II) the combination of a transfusion record and a GIB diagnosis. An isolated Hb decrease or transfusion record was not sufficient for outcome classification. Routinely available demographic, physiologic, laboratory, and disease-severity variables were extracted. Records with missing values in variables required for the final analysis were excluded before model development. Multivariable logistic regression served as the baseline model, with XGB and random forest employed as comparator models. Model performance was evaluated using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, the Brier score, and decision-curve analysis (DCA). RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV development cohort included 935 patients (GIB incidence, 10.7%), whereas the eICU-CRD validation cohort comprised 542 patients (GIB incidence, 12.7%). In the development cohort, the AUCs were 0.887 for logistic regression, 0.962 for XGB, and 0.853 for random forest. In the eICU-CRD cohort, XGB yielded an AUC point estimate of 0.873. CONCLUSIONS: This retrospective two-database analysis developed prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery. The models showed discrimination in the analyzed data; however, prospective validation using predictors measured within prespecified pre-event windows is required before clinical implementation.

This study aimed to develop prediction models for postoperative GIB following AD surgery and to externally evaluate an XGBoost (XGB) model using an independent multicenter database.

title: Post-operative multi-organ dysfunction following heart transplantation and left ventricular assist device implantation: phenotypes, trajectories, and prognostic implications-a retrospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multi-organ dysfunction syndrome (MODS) is a leading cause of mortality after heart transplantation (HTx) and left ventricular assist device (LVAD), yet its phenotypic heterogeneity remains poorly characterised. This study intends to identify and clinically validate distinct multi-organ dysfunction phenotypes following HTx and LVAD implantation, and to analyse their early prognosis using longitudinal biomarker trajectories and independent clinical adjudication. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included 68 consecutive adult patients who underwent HTx or LVAD implantation in the Cardiothoracic and Vascular Surgery Department of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, between January 2020 and June 2025. The Institutional Review Board of Tongji Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology approved this with a waiver of informed consent. We collected demographic, preoperative, and operative data from medical records. Postoperative MODS was defined by Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) criteria as dysfunction with ≥2 organ systems. Patients were followed up for inpatient, 1-, and 2-year mortality. RESULTS: vs. vs. vs. vs. vs. vs. MODS occurred in 48 of 68 patients (70.6%). It was more frequent after HTx than LVAD (77.6%52.6%, P=0.08). The most common organ dysfunctions were cardiovascular (70.6%), hepatic (60.3%), and respiratory (50.0%). Patients with MODS had significantly longer cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) duration than those without MODS (183.11±57.42138.28±29.83 min; P=0.003) and higher rates of respiratory (68.8%5.0%; P<0.001), cardiovascular (83.3%40.0%; P=0.001), and renal dysfunction (50.0%5.0%; P=0.001). After adjustment, MODS was independently associated with 2-year mortality [hazard ratio (HR) =5.47, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.07-27.9; P=0.04]. Latent class analysis (LCA) identified 2 MODS phenotypes: a high-severity/multi-system phenotype with high probabilities of renal (100%), hepatic (78%), and respiratory (72%) dysfunction, and a lower-severity/selective phenotype. The high-severity phenotype had significantly worse 2-year survival than the lower-severity phenotype (44.8%74.4%; log-rank P=0.005). CONCLUSIONS: With regard to post-cardiac surgery MODS, we report a novel trajectory-based approach that holds promise for improving early risk stratification and guiding targeted management by distinguishing high-severity multisystem from low-severity selective trajectories following HTx and LVAD implantation.

title: Balloon pulmonary angioplasty for occlusive lesions of pulmonary artery in Takayasu arteritis: A cohort study.
abstract: P BackgroundOcclusive pulmonary arterial lesions represent a major technical challenge for balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) in patients with Takayasu arteritis-associated pulmonary artery involvement. However, evidence and procedural guidance regarding BPA for occlusive lesions in this population remain limited.ObjectivesThis study aimed to summarize our center experience with BPA for occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions in patients with Takayasu arteritis and to identify potential risk factors associated with restenosis after BPA.DesignRetrospective cohort.MethodsWe retrospectively enrolled patients with Takayasu arteritis who had occlusive pulmonary arterial lesions. Lesions were morphologically categorized as subtotal or total occlusions. Total occlusions were further subclassified as cone-shaped, pouch-like, or ostial occlusions.ResultsWe included 66 patients with Takayasu arteritis, in whom 182 occlusive lesions were identified. In terms of locations, most ostial occlusions (56.52%) located lobar, while other kinds of lesions more common located segmentally. Total occlusions more frequently required guide-extension catheter support than subtotal occlusions (70.21% vs. 40.63%,<0.001). Hard-tip guidewires were required for revascularization in 53.85% of ostial occlusions, compared with only 3.13% of subtotal occlusions. Lesion-level technical success rates among attempted lesions decreased with increasing lesion complexity: 100% for subtotal occlusions, 96.0% for cone-shaped occlusions, 68.4% for pouch-like occlusions, and 43.8% for ostial occlusions. The corresponding recanalization rates among all identified lesions were 78.69%, 88.9%, 52.04%, and 10.14%, respectively. In exploratory univariable Firth penalized logistic regression, irregular anticoagulation was associated with a higher likelihood of restenosis (OR 8.51, 95% CI 1.39-60.91; P=0.021), whereas baseline hemodynamics were not associated with restenosis.ConclusionThe techniques and devices illustrated in this study might guide the BPA performance in addressing occlusive lesions.

title: Initial peripherally inserted central catheter tip position accuracy by puncture arm and associated factors in female patients with breast cancer: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: P P ObjectiveTo examine the association between puncture arm and initial peripherally inserted central catheter tip positioning accuracy in female breast cancer patients and to explore related factors associated with malposition.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 402 female breast cancer patients undergoing chemotherapy requiring peripherally inserted central catheter placement. Patients were categorized into left-arm and right-arm groups. Demographic, clinical, and operator variables were analyzed. Pre-procedural anxiety status was evaluated using the Perioperative Anxiety Scale-7. Placement accuracy was assessed radiographically. Multivariate logistic regression identified independent predictors, and model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis.ResultsIn the matched cohort, initial tip accuracy was higher in the right-arm group (90.4%) than in the left-arm group (80.8%; = 0.013). Left-arm selection, advanced age, compromised vascular condition, high pre-procedural anxiety, and limited operator experience were identified as independent factors associated with initial tip accuracy ( < 0.05). The multivariable descriptive model showed an apparent area under the curve of 0.825.ConclusionsIn this single-center retrospective cohort, right-arm puncture was associated with higher initial peripherally inserted central catheter tip positioning accuracy than left-arm puncture in female breast cancer patients. However, because breast cancer-specific factors influencing arm selection, including surgery laterality and axillary lymph node management, radiotherapy, and lymphedema-related factors, were not systematically collected, this association should not be interpreted as a causal effect of puncture side alone. These findings are hypothesis-generating and underscore the need for individualized peripherally inserted central catheter planning that considers clinical feasibility, venous condition, patient anxiety, treatment-related arm-selection factors, and operator experience.

title: [Effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement].
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This study has been registered with the U.S. National Library of Medicine Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier NCT02803294. METHODS: Data from 1012 patients who underwent TAVR at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between March 2013 and January 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients receiving conventional rehabilitation were assigned to the control group, whereas those receiving a digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation program, comprising preoperative screening and functional preparation, intraoperative eligibility assessment, postoperative stepwise rehabilitation management, and intelligent home-based rehabilitation, were assigned to the observation group. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline confounding. Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) stay and hospital stay, the incidence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR, and functional outcomes, including the five-meter walking test, six-minute walking test, and Katz index, were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: vs P vs P P P After propensity score matching, 251 patients were included in each group. Compared with the control group, the observation group had shorter postoperative ICU stays [0 (0, 1) h. 0 (0, 0) h,<0.01] and postoperative hospital stays [8 (7, 11) d. 3 (1, 7) d,<0.01]. No apparent increase in the incidence of adverse events was observed in the observation group at 30 days, 1 year, or 2 years after TAVR. The time required to complete the five-meter walking test was shorter in the observation group than in the control group at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR (all<0.01). Results of six-minute walking test and Katz index showed no significant differences between the groups (both>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation may shorten hospital stay and improve selected functional outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR without increase in postoperative cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events.

title: Prognostic Value of the Pan-Immune Inflammatory Value and Fibrinogen-To-Albumin Ratio for Amputation in Patients With Lower Extremity Arterial Disease.
abstract: p p p BackgroundLower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) remains a major cause of amputation, even after successful endovascular revascularization therapy (EVT). The prognostic associations of the pan-immune inflammatory value (PIV) and fibrinogen-to-albumin ratio (FAR) in LEAD remain unclear. This study investigated the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk and evaluated their incremental prognostic value beyond established clinical variables.MethodsIn this multicenter retrospective cohort study, 1,082 patients with LEAD who underwent EVT at four tertiary hospitals in Southwest China between January 2018 and July 2023 were analyzed. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analyses and Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to evaluate the associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk. Exploratory cut-off values were derived using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The incremental prognostic value of adding PIV and FAR to clinical variables was assessed using time-dependent ROC analysis.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 31 months, 198 (18.3%) patients experienced amputation. RCS revealed significant nonlinear associations of PIV and FAR with amputation risk (for nonlinearity < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, higher levels of both biomarkers remained independently associated with increased amputation risk (Z-PIV: HR = 1.379; Z-FAR: HR = 1.176; both< 0.001). The addition of PIV and FAR to the clinical model enhanced time-dependent discrimination; the AUC(t) increased from 0.771 to 0.819 at 1 year, 0.766 to 0.806 at 2 years, and 0.762 to 0.807 at 3 years (all adjusted< 0.001). Fine-Gray competing-risk analyses yielded consistent results after accounting for death as a competing event.ConclusionPIV and FAR were independently associated with amputation risk in patients with LEAD who underwent EVT. The addition of these biomarkers to established clinical variables provided incremental prognostic value and may offer additional prognostic information for risk stratification.

title: Personalized diagnosis and treatment of aortic diseases driven by artificial intelligence: Applications, challenges and future prospects.
abstract: Aortic aneurysm (AA) and aortic dissection (AD) are major forms of aortic disease and remain associated with substantial morbidity and mortality worldwide. Traditional diagnostic and treatment strategies largely depend on anatomical indicators, particularly maximum aortic diameter; however, such parameters are often inadequate for accurately reflecting patient-specific disease progression and rupture risk. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI), especially machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), new opportunities have emerged to overcome these limitations. This review focuses on the role of AI in advancing personalized diagnosis and management of aortic diseases. Specifically, it summarizes recent progress in four major areas. First, DL-based approaches have shown high accuracy in automated image segmentation and computer-aided diagnosis, including segmentation of the aortic lumen, intraluminal thrombus, and true and false lumens. Second, ML models incorporating biomechanical and multi-physics features have demonstrated superior performance over conventional diameter-based criteria in rupture risk assessment. Third, unsupervised learning has enabled the identification of clinically and biologically relevant molecular-imaging subtypes beyond traditional anatomical classifications. Fourth, AI has been increasingly applied to therapeutic decision-making and postoperative outcome prediction, including target identification, endovascular procedural guidance, and early detection of complications. In addition, this review discusses key barriers to clinical implementation, such as limited data quality, model overfitting, poor interpretability of DL models, and uncertainties in regulatory approval. Future advances in multicenter standardized datasets, multimodal fusion strategies, and explainable AI (XAI) are expected to accelerate the transition of aortic disease management toward AI-supported precision medicine.

title: Association of Short-Course Methylprednisolone Therapy With Early Composite Imaging Abnormalities in Patients With Early Neurological Deterioration After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early neurological deterioration (END) after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) may be accompanied by heterogeneous postprocedural imaging abnormalities. We investigated the association between short-course methylprednisolone and a study-defined early composite imaging abnormality after EVT. METHODS: This single-center retrospective analysis included 297 patients with acute ischemic stroke who developed END within 72 hours after EVT (96 treated with methylprednisolone and 201 not treated). The index time was defined as completion of the post-END treatment decision, and the first intravenous methylprednisolone dose marked the onset of exposure. The first evaluable scan obtained after END confirmation but before completion of the treatment decision was designated the index scan. All evaluable scans obtained after the index time through 72 hours after EVT were reviewed. For patients who met the primary composite outcome, the endpoint scan was the first scan showing a new abnormality or progression of a preexisting abnormality that met the specified progression criteria; for patients who did not meet the primary outcome, it was the last evaluable scan within 72 hours after EVT. Multivariate logistic regression, propensity-score analyses, a restricted analysis among patients with modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) grade 2b-3, and false discovery rate (FDR) correction were used. RESULTS: p p p p q The composite outcome occurred in 42 of 96 treated patients and 122 of 201 untreated patients (43.8% vs 60.7%;= 0.006). After multivariate adjustment, short-course methylprednisolone was associated with lower odds of the composite outcome (adjusted odds ratio, 0.46; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.27-0.80;= 0.005). The results were directionally consistent among patients with mTICI grades 2b-3 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.48; 95% CI, 0.27-0.86;= 0.013), whereas the estimate for mTICI grades 0-2a was imprecise (= 0.699). The index-to-endpoint-scan interval, endpoint imaging modality, and post-index scan frequency were comparable between groups. After FDR correction across 17 exploratory outcomes, only new or worsening cerebral edema remained statistically significant (= 0.034). Neither the 90-day 3-category modified Rankin Scale (mRS) distribution nor the comparison of mRS 0-2 remained statistically significant after correction. Safety estimates were imprecise. CONCLUSIONS: Short-course methylprednisolone was associated with lower odds of the study-defined early post-EVT composite imaging abnormality, primarily reflecting edema-related findings. This observational association did not establish functional benefit and requires prospective confirmation.

title: Ambient Carbon Monoxide as a Delayed Trigger of Acute Aortic Dissection: A Time-Stratified Case-Crossover Study in a Tropical Industrial Metropolis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) is a fatal cardiovascular emergency whose environmental triggers remain poorly understood. Although particulate air pollution has been implicated, the role of gaseous pollutants, such as carbon monoxide (CO), remains unclear. This study was performed to determine whether short-term exposure to ambient CO and other air pollutants triggers the onset of AAD. METHODS: We conducted a time-stratified case-crossover study of 798 patients with emergency department-confirmed AAD in an industrial metropolitan area from 2018 to 2021. Individual exposures to fine particulate matter (aerodynamic diameter ≤2.5 μm), particulate matter (aerodynamic diameter ≤10 μm), CO, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, sulfur dioxide, temperature, humidity, and wind speed were assigned from 24 monitoring stations. Conditional logistic regression models evaluated associations across lag 0 to 3 days, adjusting for meteorological factors. Effects were assessed using mean and interquartile range increments. RESULTS: No air pollutants were associated with AAD on the event day. However, ambient CO exhibited a strong delayed effect: at a 2-day lag, each 1-ppm increase in CO was associated with a 2.67-fold increase in AAD risk (95% CI, 1.207-5.900), and each interquartile range increase of 0.19 ppm increased risk by 113% (95% CI, 1.075-4.239). The other pollutants showed no significant associations at any lag. Apparent temperature effects in mean-based models were not confirmed by interquartile range-based analysis, indicating no robust thermal trigger. CONCLUSIONS: Ambient CO is a potent delayed trigger of acute aortic dissection, likely acting through subacute inflammatory and oxidative vascular injury rather than immediate hypoxia. These findings suggest targeted public health alerts and emission control for CO in industrialized cities.

title: Preventive Effect of a Multidisciplinary Bundle Rehabilitation Strategy Centered on Expiratory Resistance Feedback Training on Postoperative Complications in Elderly Patients With Chronic Subdural Hematoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the preventive effect of a multidisciplinary bundle rehabilitation strategy centered on expiratory resistance feedback training (MBRS) on postoperative complications in elderly patients with chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH). METHODS: A total of 258 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing surgery for CSDH were retrospectively enrolled from multiple centers. According to the actual postoperative rehabilitation protocol in this nonrandomized retrospective cohort, they were divided into the observation group (MBRS, n = 115) and the control group (routine care, n = 143). The incidences of postoperative pulmonary infection, hematoma recurrence, and lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT), as well as drainage catheter indwelling time, length of hospital stay, and hospitalization cost were compared between the 2 groups. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for key confounders was used to identify independent factors associated with complications. Propensity score matching (PSM) was additionally performed as a sensitivity analysis to control for potential confounding. RESULTS: The incidence of pulmonary infection in the observation group was 5%, significantly lower than 15% in the control group (P = 0.009). The incidence of lower extremity DVT was 3%, lower than 9% in the control group (P = 0.032). The proportion of drainage catheter indwelling ≤3 days was 86% in the observation group, higher than 64% in the control group (P < 0.001). The length of hospital stay and hospitalization cost in the observation group were significantly lower than those in the control group (all P < 0.001). Multivariate Logistic regression showed that MBRS was an independent protective factor for postoperative pulmonary infection (OR = 0.210, 95% CI: 0.073-0.604, P = 0.004) and lower extremity DVT (OR = 0.183, 95% CI: 0.039-0.850, P = 0.030). There were no significant differences in hematoma recurrence rate or the incidence of other complications between the 2 groups. CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cohort study, MBRS was associated with lower rates of postoperative pulmonary infection and lower extremity DVT, shorter drainage duration and hospital stay, and reduced costs, without increasing hematoma recurrence. Prospective RCTs are needed to confirm these findings.

METHODS: A total of 258 patients aged ≥65 years undergoing surgery for CSDH were retrospectively enrolled from multiple centers. According to the actual postoperative rehabilitation protocol in this nonrandomized retrospective cohort, they were divided into the observation group (MBRS, n = 115) and the control group (routine care, n = 143).

title: Hemodynamic Insights Into an Accessory Splenic Artery Aneurysm Arising From the Superior Mesenteric Artery.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery variations involve anomalies in origin, course, and branching. Notably, the accessory splenic artery (ASA) is a rare independent, ectopic aberrant duplication outside the celiac trunk, making its comprehension crucial for safety during endovascular interventions. CASE SUMMARY: This case report describes a 34-year-old woman with a rare splenic artery duplication, consisting of a primary splenic artery normally originating from the celiac trunk and an ASA arising from the superior mesenteric artery that harbored a distal saccular aneurysm. DISCUSSION: An ASA originating from the superior mesenteric artery and associated with aneurysm formation is an extremely rare anatomical variation. Hemodynamic evaluations based on computational fluid dynamics simulation indicated that the unique vascular configuration of this aberrant artery may predispose the aneurysm to an elevated risk of rupture. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: This type of accessory splenic artery originating from the superior mesenteric artery is reported here for the first time.

title: Numerical investigation of full crimping to 6 mm and deployment in TAVR: coupled influence of implantation depth.
abstract: To address the inadequate representation of key physical processes in numerical simulations of transcatheter aortic valve replacement, a high-fidelity mechanical analysis framework that more closely approximates clinical reality has been developed. Based on a comprehensive structural model incorporating the skirt, leaflets, and stent, this framework incorporates the clinically standard 18 Fr crimping dimension and a release mechanism based on axial extraction from the capsule. It systematically investigates the coupled effects of full crimping to clinical standards, deployment strategies, and implantation depth on the mechanical behavior of the valve. The results demonstrate that deployment approaches based on incomplete crimping and radial recoil fail to capture the pronounced spatiotemporal non-uniformity observed in realistic deployment processes. In contrast, the axial pullback mechanism induces multi-stage stress peaks and complex contact evolution, significantly enhancing the anchoring performance between the stent and the vascular wall. Furthermore, implantation depth modulates structural constraint conditions, driving a transition from localized load-bearing to global cooperative load sharing. While this improves overall stability, it also introduces potential physiological risks. Notably, quantitative analysis based on eccentricity reveals a clear correspondence between stent cross-sectional deformation and its geometric configuration. Local geometric features are shown to dominate the post-expansion shape distribution and directly influence the uniformity of radial deformation. Paravalvular leakage exhibits pronounced spatial heterogeneity, with its formation governed by the combined effects of structural interference and contact uniformity. These findings reconstruct the physical picture of the TAVR deployment process from a mechanical perspective, providing new theoretical insights for valve design optimization and patient-specific implantation strategies.

title: Stent retrievers for acute ischemic stroke: technological advances, clinical applications, and future perspectives.
abstract: Acute ischemic stroke caused by large vessel occlusion remains a leading cause of death and disability despite established reperfusion therapies. Although stent retriever-based thrombectomy has become the standard of care, outcomes are still constrained in complex occlusions and anatomically challenging cases. This review summarizes and critically appraises recent advances in stent retriever technology, thrombectomy techniques, and evidence expansion in acute ischemic stroke. Device development has progressed from first-generation retrieval systems to self-expanding stent retrievers and recent integrated retrieval-protection platforms, leading to improved clot engagement, higher first-pass reperfusion, and reduced distal embolization. Parallel refinements in procedural strategies including combined aspiration catheters, balloon guide catheters, and dual-stent techniques have enhanced recanalization efficiency and procedural control. Clinical evidence has extended thrombectomy indications beyond conventional time windows to include posterior circulation occlusion, large infarct cores, and selected medium/distal vessel occlusions under imaging-guided selection. Advances in thrombus characterization, biomaterials, surface engineering, and territory-specific devices are further enabling more tailored mechanical approaches. Nevertheless, fibrin-rich resistant thrombi, embolic complications, vascular injury, and limited high-level evidence for emerging devices remain unresolved challenges. Ongoing integration of engineering innovation and clinical data is expected to support more individualized and safer thrombectomy strategies with improved functional outcomes.
